summary:
Cajamarca has no documented trans-specific departmental law, ordinance, court ruling or incident series in the source inventory. The binding framework for trans visitors and residents of Cajamarca is Peru's national legislation, and none of the sources examined contains Cajamarca-specific content.

On 20 February 2025 the congressional Comision de Mujer y Familia approved by unanimity a dictamen merging bills 6506 and 8457, sponsored by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Munante, that would prohibit any person from entering public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite to their birth sex, with narrow exceptions for custody and for cases where required, including accompanying minors, the elderly or people with disabilities, and would oblige venues not to post ambiguous restroom signs. The text still required plenary backing at that point, and the reported trigger was a July 2023 complaint over gendered restroom labels at Lima's Jorge Chavez international airport. Activist Gianna Camacho argued the measure is discriminatory and that enforcement would rest on security staff checking the DNI to decide whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender.

On 2 April 2025 the plenary of Congress approved and waived a second vote on the dictamen of the Ley que fortalece el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los ninos y adolescentes, whose Article 5.1 prohibits persons from entering or using public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex. The IDEHPUCP human-rights institute reads Article 5 as a direct breach of equality and non-discrimination under Article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and Article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights, resting on the stereotype that trans people are more prone to enter restrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors. The institute recalls documented cases of trans people barred from public restrooms, including SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022 dismissing a trans woman's discrimination complaint against SmartFit, where the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in the DNI, and notes that gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive.

Peru recorded 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023 according to the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia. The homicide victims were 30 trans women, 23 gay men and one lesbian; 19 killings occurred in 2023 alone, 12 of them trans women, and killers were not identified in 26 of the 54 homicides, including 13 of 19 in 2023. These are national raw counts, not per-capita rates, and the source provides no denominator for comparison across departments.

In February 2023 trans sex worker Rubi Torres Silvano, 31, was kidnapped from central Lima by a 'Los Gallegos' extortion gang and killed in Carabayllo with some 30 gunshots; Priscila Aguado Huatuco, 30, was shot days earlier. Two killers were arrested in March 2023. The state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems, so hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such.
tangentialFactors:
The restroom restriction described in the February 2025 dictamen and the April 2025 statute is national in scope and applies in Cajamarca as elsewhere in Peru; enforcement would fall to venue security staff, who under the reported mechanism would check the DNI to determine whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender. A trans visitor presenting documents that do not match their presentation faces that check in any public facility in the department.

Gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive, per the IDEHPUCP analysis, so a visitor cannot rely on corrected documents to avoid the restroom rule. The 2020-2023 killing figures are national raw counts without a per-capita denominator; they cannot be used to rank Cajamarca against other departments, and the inventory contains no Cajamarca-specific violence data.
localsOnly:
Residents of Cajamarca live under the same national framework described above: Article 5.1 of the April 2025 statute bars entry to public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than birth sex, and the February 2025 dictamen carried the same prohibition with narrow exceptions for custody and for accompanying minors, elderly people or people with disabilities. Venues are obliged not to post ambiguous restroom signs under the dictamen text.

SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022 dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against SmartFit, where the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in the DNI, indicating that a private venue's DNI-based rule has survived administrative challenge. Hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such because the state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the February 2025 dictamen received plenary backing after 20 February 2025 is not resolved in the inventory; the April 2025 statute's Article 5.1 does carry the same prohibition, but the relationship between the two instruments as of the source dates is not stated.

No source in the inventory addresses enforcement practice, police conduct, healthcare access, or document-marker rules in Cajamarca specifically. The 54 homicides and 170 violation cases for 2020-2023 are national raw counts with no per-capita denominator and no departmental breakdown, so Cajamarca's position within that distribution is not sourced.
